dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: The directional update U(d,t,u)(c) = u(c) − (t/V(c)) • N(d,t,u)(c), where V is the supplied volume and N is LocalDef002.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the selected stage update appearing in the composition, cell balance, finite-segment balance, and line-agreement conclusions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: N(d,t,u)(c) = F(d,t,u)(c[d := c(d)+1]) − F(d,t,u)(c), with F defined by LocalDef003.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes the signed flux difference as the value at the next integer coordinate minus the value at the current coordinate.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: F(d,t,u)(c) = rule(d,c,t,j ↦ u(c[d := j])).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The rule receives the direction, full cell index, duration, and entire integer-indexed state line through that cell. These values supply both boundary terms and the cell flux difference.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: Maps every stage (d,t) to its update U(d,t,·), then applies these updates to the initial state in list order.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the full evolution and the intermediate state obtained after the prefix before the selected stage.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given real t and v and vectors a and f, returns a − (t/v) • f.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the exact update formula, including division by the individual cell volume and subtraction of the scaled flux difference.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: Applies a finite list of state transformations from left to right, starting with the supplied state.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Determines that the first listed stage acts first and that an empty stage list acts as the identity.

dependency_coverage.name: AddCommGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: An abelian additive group structure, with zero, addition, additive inverses, and subtraction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the algebra on E needed for differences and finite sums; no order or norm on E is assumed.

dependency_coverage.name: AddCommGroup.toAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains the commutative additive monoid underlying an abelian group.

dependency_coverage.name: AddCommGroup.toAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains the additive group underlying an abelian additive group.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the inherited group operations used throughout the expressions in E.

dependency_coverage.name: AddGroup.toSubNegMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains the additive monoid, negation, and subtraction structure of an additive group.

dependency_coverage.name: AddMonoid.toAddZeroClass

dependency_coverage.name: AddZero.toZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the zero element from an addition-with-zero structure.

binders: Universally quantify a type D of coordinate directions, with decidable equality, and a type E equipped with an abelian additive group structure and a real module structure.
Write C = D → Z for the set of cells. Universally quantify V : C → R.
Universally quantify rule : D → C → R → (Z → E) → E and a finite ordered list S of pairs in D × R.
Universally quantify the initial state u₀ : C → E.
Within the conclusion, universally quantify finite lists B and A of stages, a direction d ∈ D, and a real t, subject to S = B ++ [(d,t)] ++ A. Define u = T(B,u₀), so u depends on V, rule, B, and u₀.
For each such decomposition, the cell balance quantifies every c ∈ C; the segment balance quantifies every base b ∈ C, start s ∈ Z, and length n ∈ N.
For each such decomposition, the line-agreement assertion quantifies every other state v : C → E and base b ∈ C, and then every integer j.
hypotheses: For every cell c ∈ C, V(c) > 0.
S is not the empty list.
For every direction d ∈ D, there exists a real t such that (d,t) occurs in S. This witness may depend on d.
Every stage (d,t) occurring in S has t > 0.
The conclusions concerning a selected stage are conditional on the exact list equality S = B ++ [(d,t)] ++ A.
The line-agreement conclusion is conditional on u(b[d := j]) = v(b[d := j]) for every j ∈ Z.
conclusions: The list S is nonempty, every direction occurs in S with some real duration, and every occurring stage has strictly positive duration. These three conclusions repeat the corresponding hypotheses.
For every decomposition S = B ++ [(d,t)] ++ A, with u = T(B,u₀), the full evolved state satisfies T(S,u₀) = T(A,U(d,t,u)) as an equality of functions C → E.
For every such decomposition and every cell c, V(c) • U(d,t,u)(c) = V(c) • u(c) − t • N(d,t,u)(c).

For every such decomposition, every base b, every integer s, and every natural n, put c_k = b[d := s+k], interpreting k as an integer. Then Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} V(c_k) • U(d,t,u)(c_k) = Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} V(c_k) • u(c_k) − t • (F(d,t,u)(b[d := s+n]) − F(d,t,u)(b[d := s])).
For every such decomposition, every other state v, and every base b, if u and v agree at b[d := j] for all integers j, then U(d,t,u) and U(d,t,v) agree at b[d := j] for all integers j.
mathematical_definitions: For c ∈ C, c[d := j] denotes the cell whose coordinate at d is j and whose other coordinates equal those of c. The unit forward shift is c⁺ᵈ = c[d := c(d)+1].
The symbol • denotes the given real scalar multiplication on E. All vector differences and finite sums use E's abelian additive group operations.
F(d,t,u)(c) = rule(d,c,t,j ↦ u(c[d := j])). Thus the rule's state argument is the entire line indexed by absolute integer coordinate j, while c remains a separate argument.
U(d,t,u)(c) = u(c) − (t/V(c)) • N(d,t,u)(c). The same V and rule are used in every occurrence of U, F, N, and T.

T([],u) = u, and T((d,t)::L,u) = T(L,U(d,t,u)). Consequently, for S = [(d₁,t₁),…,(d_m,t_m)], T(S,u₀) is obtained by applying these updates in the listed order, each to the state produced by its predecessors.
Each finite-segment sum runs over natural indices k with 0 ≤ k < n. Its cells have direction-d coordinates s through s+n−1, and its two flux evaluations have direction-d coordinates s and s+n.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any real vector space E, any direction type D with decidable equality, any strictly positive real volume assigned to every integer-coordinate cell, and any rule assigning an E-valued result from a direction, cell, real duration, and complete state line, consider a nonempty finite ordered schedule of positive-duration directional stages covering every direction. For every initial state, the schedule retains those three stated properties. At every occurrence of a stage in the schedule, let the current state be the result of applying the preceding stages. The final state is exactly the result of applying that stage to the current state and then applying the remaining stages. At each cell, this stage changes the volume-weighted state by minus the duration times the forward difference of the rule-defined flux. On every finite consecutive segment in that direction, these changes sum to minus the duration times the terminal flux minus the initial flux. Finally, if another state agrees with the current state along an entire line in the selected direction, the two states also agree along that line after applying the same selected stage.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Although D is not explicitly equipped with a finiteness or nonemptiness instance, a finite schedule covering all directions forces D to have finitely many elements, and a nonempty list of pairs in D × R forces D to be inhabited. For infinite or empty D, the schedule hypotheses cannot all hold, so the implication is vacuous.
Coverage requires at least one stage per direction. It does not require exactly one stage per direction, distinct stage pairs, equal durations, a prescribed order, or a prescribed total duration.

The direction and duration in the stage-specific conclusion must arise from a decomposition of the given schedule. For tuples that do not give that decomposition, the conditional assertion imposes no requirement.
The volume is strictly positive at every cell, not merely at cells in a selected segment. It may vary arbitrarily with the cell; no uniform lower bound or geometric interpretation is assumed.

Cells comprise all functions D → Z, and states are arbitrary functions on all these cells. There are no spatial boundary restrictions, periodicity assumptions, finite-support conditions, or summability assumptions.
The segment length may be zero. In that case both sums are zero and the two endpoint flux evaluations coincide, so the segment identity is trivial.

The rule is arbitrary and may depend on the full cell index, direction, duration, and entire state line. No finite stencil, continuity, linearity, consistency with a differential equation, stability, or positivity preservation is encoded.

The line-agreement conclusion concerns one selected directional update using the same volume and rule. It requires agreement on the entire integer line and does not assert locality to a finite neighborhood or preservation of line agreement by the full schedule.
The finite-segment balance includes a boundary-flux difference. It does not assert that the segment's weighted sum remains unchanged, or that a total sum over the full grid exists or is conserved.
E need not be finite-dimensional, normed, ordered, or nontrivial. In the zero vector space the vector equalities hold trivially, while the schedule and volume hypotheses remain required.
The first three conclusions restate assumptions. The proposition does not construct a covering schedule or prove positive durations from properties of the update.

The words cell volume, state, duration, and flux describe argument roles; the declaration does not supply geometric cells, physical units, a time-dependent physical solution, or an accuracy or convergence claim.
